thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Canary rollout 2026-03-14T10:05Z (model: rwd-v2.1-canary) triggered SLO breach. p95 latency jumped from 210ms -> 1200ms, p99 from 720ms -> 3.4s; streaming stalls observed (consumer-ack backlog). Routing: canary=12% traffic.

maya_oncall: Paging SRE oncall. seeing p99 tail blow up after the canary ramp. Streaming sessions showing repeated `recv` timeouts. :warning:

eli_runtime: I can see the same in traces — KV cache miss rate spiked ~6x for canary shards. Many requests hit the longer attention path.

sam_platform: Confirming: autoscale didn't kick for the canary nodes because max_pool=8 and we saturated per-GPU concurrency. Might be backpressure in the queue.

jess_sre: Quick triage plan: 1) stop ramp (hold new traffic), 2) redirect canary -> stable (rollback route), 3) increase canary pool size OR disable canary batching, 4) collect traces and attach to ticket.

maya_oncall: Doing step 1 now — pausing rollout via control plane.

maya_oncall: `POST https://control-plane.internal/rollouts/2026-0314-canary/pause` -> 200 OK. Traffic hold confirmed.

ryan_eng: I have a simple route flip ready if we need full rollback: `PATCH /routes/canary -> target=stable` (I can run in 30s).

eli_runtime: While paused, look at streaming stalls: it looks like the model variant uses a new kv-sharding strategy that increases first-token time under certain prefix patterns. That explains sudden tail latency for some customer prompt shapes.

maya_oncall: Running diagnostics: `kubectl logs -l app=inference -c runtime --since=5m | grep "stall" | tail -n 50` — grabbing samples.

jess_sre: Also alerting CS about potential customer impact. Tara, can you surface active customer sessions?

tara_cs: Notifying affected customers: a small number of streaming sessions (est. < 10 customers, mostly high-throughput). Drafting message now.

sam_platform: I can temporarily bump canary pool to 20 to see if capacity helps. Doing `curl -XPOST https://infra.internal/pools/canary/resize -d '{"size":20}'`

maya_oncall: Wait on resizing — first try rolling canary back to previous model binary (rwd-v2.0) at routing level. Prefer graceful rollback over resize because this looks model-behavior-related.

ryan_eng: Rolling back routing now: `PATCH https://control-plane.internal/routes/canary` body: ```{"target_model":"rwd-v2.0","drain_timeout_s":30}```

ryan_eng: Patch returned 202 Accepted. Traffic flip in progress.

incident-bot: Update: Canary traffic routing change propagated to region-us-east-1 in ~18s.

eli_runtime: I'm watching p99. Initial drop seen — p99 down from 3.4s -> 1.1s within the first minute. p95 also trending down.

maya_oncall: I'm going to scale down the canary pool back to nominal after we confirm stable performance to avoid extra spend.

jess_sre: Good. Please capture before/after traces and update the incident ticket with the KV-miss evidence and model-commit hash for rwd-v2.1. We'll need a rollback postmortem item.

tara_cs: Customer msg sent: short note that we detected increased tail latency for streaming after a canary model change, we rolled traffic back to stable and are monitoring. Will follow up with timeline.

sam_platform: After the flip, I still see intermittent stalls for a few sessions — likely sessions that remained sticky to canary workers until their tokens expired. Draining currently.

maya_oncall: On-call handoff in 25 mins — Jess will take over if this stays in monitoring. Handing off: all mitigation actions executed (pause -> rollback), rank-1 mitigations done.

jess_sre: I'll take it. Next steps: 1) run a targeted A/B against rwd-v2.1 in a sandbox for the sequence shapes that blew up; 2) add an alert for KV-miss delta > 3x during rollouts; 3) add a short-circuit in routing to fallback to stable when p99 > 2s for 2 consecutive mins.

eli_runtime: For immediate forensic: saving representative traces and KV cache stats to the incident ticket. `attach /tmp/canary_kv_dumps/*.json` (I'll upload).

maya_oncall: Metrics update: 10m after rollback p95 = 230ms, p99 = 360ms, streaming stall count down to baseline. No customer escalations so far. Marking incident as mitigated, moving to monitoring.

incident-bot: Incident status changed -> mitigated by maya_oncall. Severity: Sev3 (customer impact limited).

ryan_eng: Filing follow-up: create postmortem and add action items: model canary validation for KV behavior, add conservative canary ramp for models that change sharding, and an automated route rollback if p99 > 2s.

tara_cs: I'll follow up with customers for post-incident detail if they ask; ticket updated.

jess_sre: handoff complete. Leaving notes in runbook: `if canary causes p99 spike, first pause rollout, then route flip, then consider pool resize only if traffic-related`.

maya_oncall: Thanks team. Monitoring for 30 more minutes then closing the page. :thumbsup:
